description: RT-07 fairness scenarios; native bulk_vs_small_streams has a separate-process diagnostic runner, while other cells and qualification remain unimplemented

fairness_contract.latency_basis: completion minus scheduled dispatch; retain rejections, timeouts and unfinished calls separately
fairness_contract.measurement_unit: per workload class and per endpoint, never aggregate throughput alone

per_workload_class.queue_delay_nanos: {p99: u64, max: u64} | null (full outbound/server queue not observable)
per_workload_class.observed_client_pool_wait_nanos: {samples: u64, p99: u64, max: u64} | null
per_workload_class.p99_latency_nanos: u64 | null (unstarted overflow or non-timeout failure lacks deadline-valued latency)
per_workload_class.scheduling_lag_samples_nanos: u64[] | null (all offered small calls, including unstarted)

per_endpoint.post_drain_probe_success: bool (admission probe, not a permit count)

metric_sources.rejected_calls_by_reason: fairness runner maps Status.code().name() to canonical RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED and LoadRecord.rejected_calls to QUEUE_OVERFLOW; independent client/server LifecycleObserver.on_rejection counts are diagnostic, not deduplicated
metric_sources.queue_delay_nanos: null: client on_queue_wait measures only pool acquisition, and on_server_queue_wait has no emitter; full outbound-to-TCP/server queue delay not exposed
metric_sources.observed_client_pool_wait_nanos: LifecycleObserver.on_queue_wait (per class, count + p99/max), distinct from LoadRecord scheduling lag and full outbound queue wait
metric_sources.scheduling_lag_p99_nanos: LoadRecord.scheduling_lags_nanos from actual spawned task start minus scheduled Poisson arrival for dispatched small calls, or generator decision minus arrival for unstarted overflows; null for closed-loop bulk
metric_sources.p99_latency_nanos: Raw scheduled-relative small samples retain every dispatched outcome and deadline-valued timeouts; required p99 is null on unstarted QUEUE_OVERFLOW or early non-timeout statuses (not deadline-valued), and the run fails when calls remain unfinished; bulk p99 is likewise null on non-timeout failures
metric_sources.client_cpu_seconds: client process ResourceSnapshot user+system CPU delta after warmup through post-drain probe
metric_sources.server_cpu_seconds: server process ResourceSnapshot user+system CPU delta after warmup through shutdown
metric_sources.client_start_rss_bytes: client process ResourceSnapshot.current_rss_bytes after warmup; missing capture fails run
metric_sources.server_start_rss_bytes: server process ResourceSnapshot.current_rss_bytes after warmup; missing capture fails run
metric_sources.client_peak_rss_bytes: client process ResourceSnapshot resident high-water mark through load and post-drain; includes warmup because process-lifetime gauge
metric_sources.server_peak_rss_bytes: server process ResourceSnapshot resident high-water mark through shutdown; includes warmup because process-lifetime gauge
metric_sources.client_active_permits_peak: null: client transport semaphore occupancy has no public gauge
metric_sources.server_active_permits_peak: null: server transport semaphore occupancy has no public gauge; admitted-call observer counts are not the same measurement
metric_sources.client_active_permits_post_drain: null: successful probe is not an exact client permit count
metric_sources.server_active_permits_post_drain: null: successful probe is not an exact server permit count
metric_sources.client_byte_budget_allocated_bytes_peak: null: no exact high-water gauge; client sampled lower bound uses ByteBudgetTracker.allocated() at callbacks and 5ms polling
metric_sources.server_byte_budget_allocated_bytes_peak: null: no exact high-water gauge; server sampled lower bound uses ByteBudgetTracker.allocated() at callbacks and 5ms polling
metric_sources.client_byte_budget_allocated_bytes_post_: shared client ByteBudgetTracker.allocated() after bounded drain

ci_smoke_contract.source: docs/resource-budgets.md section 7.3 (F-1 through F-6, O-1 through O-3)
ci_smoke_contract.rss: recorded, not threshold-gated in PR runs; shared-process RSS cannot attribute an endpoint
ci_smoke_contract.percentiles: 32-call deterministic loopback regression, not statistically qualified p99

execution_status.scenario_file: rpc-bench fairness --scenario rpc-bench/scenarios/fairness.json executes only native/native bulk_vs_small_streams in separate processes; five other cells remain declarative
execution_status.missing_metric_policy: null with an explicit unsupported_metrics reason and qualification.qualified=false; --require-qualified exits nonzero after writing the report; never substitute zero, sampled lower bounds or aggregate QPS
available_now: scheduled Poisson 128-byte unary RPCs overlap repeating finite 64 x 64KiB server streams at bounded concurrency, after discarded mixed warmup
per-class offered/dispatched/success/failure counts, typed RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED and QUEUE_OVERFLOW, deadline-valued timeout samples, raw latency/scheduling lag and sampled client pool wait
separate-process client/server baseline RSS, lifetime peak RSS, CPU deltas, observed byte-budget sample lower bounds and exact post-drain byte accounting
bounded CI smoke tests for competition, observed client queue wait and post-drain admission probes
required_before_qualification: runnable slow reader/writer, idle peer, reset storm and overload cells; open-loop offered load for every required workload class
client outbound-to-TCP and server queue delays, full offered-call failure latencies including unstarted QUEUE_OVERFLOW
public client/server active-permit and byte-budget high-water gauges (sampled allocated() peaks are not exact)
paired randomized dedicated-host native/tonic-pbrs runs, confidence intervals and RSS growth review; target_thresholds are proposals, not gates

scenarios.name: Bulk Streaming vs Small Unary RPCs
scenarios.description: Mix multi-megabyte bulk server streams with scheduled 128-byte unary probes; evaluate per-class p99, scheduler/client queue wait, explicit rejections and post-drain budget recovery, not total QPS.

scenarios.name: Slow Reader Flow-Control Isolation
scenarios.description: Pause application response consumption on separate streaming connections to withhold flow-control capacity; verify exact eventual delivery and fast-call p99 on an independent connection.

scenarios.name: Slow Writer Inbound Drip Isolation
scenarios.description: Drip whole client-stream messages at fixed intervals while keeping the upload open; verify accepted order, fast-call p99 and permit release after close.

scenarios.name: Idle Connection Fleet Contention
scenarios.description: Keep 100 established HTTP/2 peers idle while scheduled active calls use separate connections; record per-class p99, queue wait and idle-connection RSS overhead.

scenarios.name: HTTP/2 Rapid Reset Storm Isolation
scenarios.description: Generate measured RST_STREAM(CANCEL) traffic during scheduled valid unary calls; retain reset counts, explicit outcomes, legitimate p99 and post-storm budget/permit recovery.

scenarios.name: Overload Budget Rejection Without Silent Buffering
scenarios.description: Hold RPC slots or transport byte permits while offering an open-loop burst. Record every outcome, immediate RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED status citing the violated limit, admitted-call p99 and post-release recovery; rejected calls must not reach the application handler.
